summary: Rear mark of the Liston range on the Delaware River: a wrought-iron tower first lit at Port Penn in 1877, moved here in 1904-06; now privately owned per LighthouseFriends.

access.note: The lighthouse and dwellings are privately owned; grounds, dwellings and tower closed (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: As the Port Penn Range Rear Light, first lit 2 April 1877 at Hazel Glen, west of Port Penn
Abandoned Port Penn tower taken down and re-erected at the Liston site by contract; temporary lights from 25 October 1904
Re-lit at the new site on 15 May 1906
Second-order range lens replaced the reflector light on 10 November 1906
Keeper's dwelling, barn, oil house and privy completed by August 1907
Keepers extinguished a fire near the station that threatened nearby buildings (fiscal 1921 report)
Keepers detailed as attendants at the Lighthouse Service exhibit at the Philadelphia exposition
Head keeper retired in 1933; station then fully automated (LighthouseFriends). The nomination places the electrification of the lamp in the mid-1930s
Thirty-year lease to the Delaware River & Bay Lighthouse Foundation; surrendered 2007
Offered at a General Services Administration online auction; closed 20 May 2013 with a high bid of $22,003
Bought by a private owner; tower and dwellings in one ownership again

corrections.field: USLHS place record: Year Tower Established
corrections.why: The tower was first lit at Port Penn on 2 April 1877 (NRHP; LighthouseFriends) and was moved and re-erected here in 1904-06. The place record's 1904 is the move, not the first lighting. Noted for the archive, not a change to this record.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1906 and the archive's 1904 are both right for different events: 1904 is when the tower was moved and re-erected at the Liston site, 1906 when it was re-lit here. The first lighting, 2 April 1877, was at Port Penn.
Not resolved. The archive's place record marks the light as not an active aid; the 2018 Delaware Bay association page says nothing about the rear light's current lighting.

notes_for_editor: Status is unresolved: the USLHS place record says active_aton false; the 2018 DBLHKFA page says the Coast Guard owns the small parcel under the tower (the NRHP, 1978, says the Coast Guard retains ownership of the light); LighthouseFriends says the tower and oil house were sold at a GSA auction in 2013 and a private owner bought them in 2020, and that the dwellings are private. The story reports the disagreement. Whether the rear light still shows is not established by any source read. Height: the NRHP says 120 feet from base to focal plane (36.6 m); the USLHS record gives 171 ft tower height and 176 ft focal height (the station record gives 54 m). Assistant house date: LighthouseFriends 1910 at $5,851 (after a March 1908 inspection found the assistant's family living upstairs in the keeper's dwelling) vs NRHP 'about 1913'. Electrification: LighthouseFriends 1930 vs NRHP mid-1930s. NRHP OCR prints the station name as 'Listen'; the official name is Liston. Source 3 (Commissioner, fiscal 1921): the fire entry is in the Fourth District list, on printed page 60 by the OCR page header; the scan page 665 image was not viewed. The fire is undated beyond the fiscal year (July 1920 to June 1921). Source 4 (1912-1917 Bulletin index) lists 'Listons Range Rear, change in illuminant' at page 70 but gives no year or new illuminant, so the story does not date the change. The local corpus has a 1913 Bulletin (PDF p.22) list of 'Important changes in aids to navigation' in which 'Listons Range Rear, Delaware' appears among entries headed 'Illuminant changed to incandescent oil vapor'; the OCR interleaves columns, so the heading is not verified and the story does not use it. The event for the change was dropped from the record until it is checked on the page image. The 1906 Lighthouse Board report is quoted by LighthouseFriends; the 1904-1906 Board reports are not in the local corpus. Newspaper search of Delaware papers (Chronicling America, 1904-1935) failed with a service error and was not retried, so local press coverage of the 1904 move, the 1921 fire and any storms is unchecked. The keeper dispute of 1919 is from LighthouseFriends, which quotes Service records; the story paraphrases it without the source's racial slur. Private owners named by LighthouseFriends (the 1913 auction buyer, the 2020 owner, the dwelling family) are not named here: they are private people. Harry Spencer Jr. (born at the station in 1920, a private person) is not named. Wikipedia was consulted for leads only and is not cited. The roster lines carry the USLHS person slugs as printed by roster.py --json.
